title: Acquisition of murine splenic myeloid cells for protein and gene expression profiling by advanced flow cytometry and CITE-seq
protocol: Euthanize mice using an institutionally approved method.
Place the mouse right side down on the dissection mat, and spray fur with 80% ethanol to disinfect.
Make a horizontal incision in the skin on the left thorax just below the ribcage.
Dissect through peritoneum until the spleen is visible.
Carefully grasp the spleen with forceps and lift it out of the abdomen.
Ensure complete detachment from the pancreas by cutting the splenic blood vessels.
Place the spleen into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL of cold PBS.
Store the Eppendorf tube on ice.
Dispose of the mouse cadaver.
Remove the spleen from PBS using blunt forceps and place it into a fresh Eppendorf tube.
Inject 1 mL of collagenase D Digestion Buffer at 18°C–23°C into each spleen using multiple puncture locations.
Incubate the spleen immersed in digestion buffer in an Eppendorf tube in a 37°C water bath for 30 min.
Transfer contents of the splenic digestion onto a 70 μm cell strainer over a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Gently mash the spleen through the strainer using a rubber plunger of a 5 mL syringe.
Wash the strainer with 10 mL of PBS at 18°C–23°C using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Centrifuge splenocytes at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend cells from one spleen in 1 mL of Ammonium-Chloride-Potassium (ACK) lysis buffer.
Incubate on ice for 2 min.
Process only one spleen through one cell strainer to ensure maximal cell yield.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C after adding 10 mL of PBS.
Resuspend cells from one spleen in 1 ml of PBS.
Count cells using trypan blue and a counting slide if absolute counts are required.
Replace PBS with plain RPMI1640 media in digestion buffer and washes if cell viability is below 80%.
Vortex compensation beads for 30 seconds to break up aggregates.
Pipette 20 μL of bead solution into empty FACS tubes.
Add 80 μL of FACS buffer to each tube containing the bead solution.
Pipette 1 μL of the corresponding antibody to each tube.
Incubate on ice or at 4°C in the dark for 15 minutes.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to each tube after incubation.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully decant supernatant from each tube.
Resuspend tubes in 200 μL of FACS buffer.
Keep compensation controls on ice or at 4°C in the dark until acquisition.
Incubate single cells with fluorescence-tagged antibodies.
Keep all antibodies and buffers on ice while preparing antibody solutions.
Prepare antibody solutions fresh within the hour before sample incubation.
Pipette approximately 5 × 10^6 splenocytes into FACS tubes for the unstained sample and each experimental sample tube.
Pipette approximately 2 × 10^6 splenocytes into a live/dead single stain control tube.
Transfer half of live/dead single stain cells into a fresh Eppendorf tube.
Place the Eppendorf tube on a heat plate set at 50°C for 10 min to initiate cell death.
Prepare a Fc block/FVS solution as outlined.
Incubate samples for 10 minutes.
Place dead cells on ice for 2 minutes.
Transfer dead cells back to the original live/dead Eppendorf tube containing live cells.
Centrifuge live/dead single stain and experimental sample tubes at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant supernatant from the tubes.
Add 50 μL of live/dead/Fc-block cocktail to experimental samples and live/dead single stains.
Incubate on ice or at 4°C in the dark for 15 minutes.
Prepare antibody cocktail using desired concentrations of each antibody in 40 μL FACS buffer + 10 μL Brilliant Stain buffer per sample.
Add 1 mL of PBS to all tubes incubated with live/dead/Fc-block cocktail and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant supernatant.
Resuspend live/dead single stain control in 400 μL of FACS buffer and leave on ice or at 4°C in the dark until acquisition.
Resuspend experimental samples each in 50 μL of antibody cocktail.
Incubate samples on ice or at 4°C in the dark for 20 min.
Add 1 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant supernatants.
Resuspend cell pellets in 400 μL of FACS buffer and store on ice or at 4°C in the dark until acquisition.
Vortex and strain cells through a FACS tube microstrainer using a disposable transfer pipette immediately before loading onto cytometer.
Manipulate PMT voltages to adjust forward and side scatter (FSC/SSC).
Reflect 3 times of the robust standard deviation (rSD) for each channel to ensure comparable fluorophore sensitivity across all channels.
Use 3 × rSD to set PMT voltages for signal detection while reducing electronic noise.
For dim signals, use up to 10 × rSD to detect appropriate signal.
Derive manipulated rSD values from pre-gated lymphocytes using the forward and side scatter gate.
Begin acquisition of single stain compensation controls with the unstained sample according to automatic compensation workflow instructions.
Vortex compensation tubes for 3–5 seconds before acquisition to resuspend beads.
Acquire 5000 total events for each compensation control.
Ensure a sufficiently high stain index in compensation controls for successful automatic compensation.
Perform automatic compensation calculation after acquiring compensation controls.
Vortex experimental samples before acquisition to ensure cells are in solution.
Acquire at least 2 × 10^6 events of FSC/SSC lymphocyte gate from each sample for adequate resolution.
Export flow cytometry standard (FCS) files.
Verify automatic compensation using Kaluza software.
Correct automatic compensation if necessary.
Carry out a quality control of the compensation matrix.
Analyze flow cytometric data using Kaluza software.
Import FCS files to the analysis software of choice.
Generate a FSC-A/SSC-A bivariate plot.
Gate lymphocyte populations on the bivariate plot.
Generate a FSC-A/FSC-H bivariate plot.
Gate single cells along a linear, 45 degree line.
Create a bivariate plot for each used channel with the channel on the X axis.
Highlight all plots and change the Y axes to the first channel.
Correct compensation as required if typical patterns suggesting overcompensation or undercompensation are observed.
Change Y axes to the next channel and repeat compensation correction.
Repeat for all channels.
Identify myeloid cells based on gating strategy demonstrated in Figures 2 and 3.
Isolate live, single, leukocytes.
Exclude non-target populations such as T-cells (CD3+).
Exclude non-target populations such as B-cells (CD19+).
From CD45+ cells, exclude B cells and NKT/T cells.
Validate Ly6G+ neutrophils based on CD11b expression.
Identify pDCs as PDCA1+ cells.
Delineate macrophages from PDCA1- cells based on F4/80 expression and absence of Ly6C- and CD11c-.
Identify monocytes from CD3-CD19-Ly6G-PDCA1- cells as Ly6C+.
Further identify monocyte diversity through differential expression of CD11b and CD172a.
Identify cDCs from CD3-CD19-Ly6G-PDCA1-Ly6C- cells based on MHC-II+ and CD11c+ expression.
Subdivide cDCs into cDC1 (XCR1+CD172a-) and cDC2 (CD172a+XCR1-) cells.
Verify identity of cDC1 by expression of CD24 and CD11b, respectively.
Verify identity of cDC2 by expression of CD11b and absence of CD24, respectively.
Further subdivide cDC1 and cDC2 into CD4+ and CD4- cells.
Resuspend splenocytes at 1 × 108 cells/mL in FACS buffer in a round bottomed 5 mL tube.
Add 5 μL/mL of biotin conjugated anti-TCRb to the cell solution.
Add 5 μL/mL of biotin conjugated anti-CD19 to the cell solution.
Incubate for 10 min at 18°C–23°C.
Add 75 μL of RapidSpheresTM magnetic beads to the cell solution.
Incubate for 2.5 min at 18°C–23°C.
Place the tube in an EasySepTM magnet and incubate for 2.5 min.
Carefully decant the supernatant with the myeloid cells into a new FACS tube.
Set aside a small quantity of cells for unstained and single stain controls.
Stain cells with Fc-block at a dilution of 1:100 and live/dead cell stain at a dilution of 1:250 for 20 minutes on ice.
Wash the stained cells with 1 mL PBS, then centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL FACS buffer and stain with anti-MHCII-APC-Cy7 (dilution 1:400) and anti-CD11c-PE-Cy7 (dilution 1:200) for 20 minutes on ice.
Wash cells with 3 mL FACS buffer, then centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL FACS buffer.
Set up cell sorter PMT voltages and compensation using unstained and single stained cells.
Determine cells and eliminate debris based on forward scatter height (FCS-H) vs side scatter height (SSC-H).
Identify single cells by analyzing forward scatter area vs forward scatter height (FSC-A vs FSC-H) and side scatter area vs side scatter height (SSC-A vs SSC-H).
Determine live cells as those negative for the live/dead stain.
Determine cDCs as MHCII+CD11c+ cells.
Sort cDCs into a FACS tube containing 500 μL of 100% fetal calf serum (FCS).
Dilute sorted cells with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellet from the sort in Cell Staining Buffer (1 ×10ˆ6 mouse cells in 49.5 μL) in a FACS tube.
Add 0.5 μL of TruStain FcX™ PLUS (anti-mouse CD16/32) antibody per 49.5 μL cell suspension.
Incubate for 10 min at 4°C.
Prepare antibody pool using titrated amount (up to 1 μg of each TotalSeq-A antibody).
Add Cell Staining Buffer to make the volume of the antibody pool 50 μL for each 50 μL cell suspension.
Centrifuge the antibody pool at 1,400 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Carefully pipette out the antibody pool without touching the bottom of the tube.
Add 50 μL of antibody pool to each 50 μL of cell suspension.
Incubate for 30 min on ice.
Wash with 3 mL Cell Staining Buffer and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant.
Repeat wash twice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 250 μL Cell Staging Buffer.
Wash thoroughly after oligo-tagged antibody staining to reduce background noise from unbound antibodies.
Spike in cells that are negative for the antibody-specific epitopes as an internal control for antibody background noise.
Prepare all necessary reagents for GEM generation as outlined in the 10× Genomics Chromium User Guide.
Manually count cells and ensure that cell viability is above 80%.
Consult the table on page 33 of the Cell Multiplexing User Guide to determine the appropriate volume of cells to add for a particular concentration.
Prepare gene expression and CITE-seq libraries by following the BioLegend TotalSeq-A protocol.
Follow the 10x Genomics Chromium User Guide.
Start GEM generation immediately after oligo-tagged antibody staining.
Ensure sample viability is greater than 80% before starting GEM generation.
Include ADT additive primer in the cDNA amplification mix according to the TotalSeq-A protocol.
Save low molecular weight fragments in the supernatant of the post-amplification clean-up.
Pool gene expression and CITE-seq libraries at a 10% and 90% molar ratio respectively.
Sequence the pooled libraries according to desired sequencing depth.
Generate >20,000 gene expression reads per cell for two samples targeting 15,000 cells each using a NovaSeq SP 100 cycle sequencing run.
Increase the pooling proportion of CITE-seq libraries if more antibodies are used to ensure adequate read numbers.
Ensure minimum recommended sequencing depth of 20,000 reads per cell for gene expression libraries and 5,000 reads per cell for barcoded antibody libraries.
Adjust read depth per cell as needed when using a higher number of barcoded antibodies or highly abundant proteins such as CD45.
Use the recommended configuration for sequencing: Read1 – 28 bases, Index1 – 10 bases, Index2 – 10 bases, Read2 – 90 bases.
Process raw sequencing data using Cell Ranger software to generate fastq files for each sample.
Generate count tables from the processed data, which contain both gene expression and CITE-seq feature information.
Demultiplex raw sequencing data from the Illumina platform using the BCL format.
Convert demultiplexed data into fastq files.
Use the 10× Genomics Cell Ranger mkfastq pipeline for conversion.
Create a comma-separated table specifying flowcell lane, sample names, and indexes used.
Add 'ATCT' to the end of each index sequence for CITE-seq library indexes in the SimpleCSV samplesheet.
Provide the sequence 'GTGTAGATCT' in an additional 'Index2' column for single-indexed CITE-seq library fragments.
